explicit_definitions_given: Libertarian free will: uncaused prime mover, capacity to do otherwise
Compatibilist freedom: voluntary action under divine determination
Evil as privation vs. evil as substance

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Preemptive - anticipates objections by redefining key terms (e.g., 'willingness')
objections_raised: If God is ultimate cause of all choices, human moral responsibility collapses
The distinction between ultimate and proximate causality is collapsed
The agent is reduced from primary moral agent to secondary conduit

appeals_to_authority: Augustine's texts (De Libero Arbitrio, De Praedestinatione Sanctorum)

philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: The problem of evil, divine sovereignty, free will, moral responsibility

summary_of_core_decisions: The text presents a dialectical progression where Augustine's two major works are framed as strategic responses to specific heresies (Manicheanism and Pelagianism). The core decision is to subordinate human moral agency to divine sovereignty, which the text argues is theologically coherent but philosophically fatal to libertarian responsibility. The analysis concludes that this synthesis leaves an unresolved tension between divine determinism and human freedom.
